title: Right Verdict, Right Reason? An Execution-Grounded Study of Whether LLM Vulnerability Detectors Understand Vulnerabilities
abstract: arXiv:2611.28584v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to detect vulnerabilities, and their benchmark scores are often read as evidence that they understand the vulnerabilities they report. We test this reading against program execution. For 515 C and C++ functions from BigVul and PrimeVul whose vulnerability we reproduce with a proof of concept, we identify the line at which the fault occurs and the statements on which the faulting run depended. These facts ground a ladder of five tests, from telling a vulnerable function from its fixed version, through locating the fault and reacting to its removal, to judging execution-confirmed edits and predicting the outcome of a concrete run. Each test is paired with a baseline that needs no understanding, such as a rule that picks lines with risky calls, and we repeat the study on 195 vulnerabilities published after the training cutoffs of the models. translated_title: 判决正确，理由也正确吗？一项基于程序执行的研究：LLM漏洞检测器是否真正理解漏洞
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于漏洞检测，其基准测试分数常被解读为模型理解所报告漏洞的证据。我们通过程序执行来检验这一解读。针对来自BigVul和PrimeVul的515个C和C++函数（这些函数的漏洞我们均已用概念验证成功重现），我们确定了故障发生的代码行以及出错运行所依赖的语句。这些事实构成了一组由五个测试组成的递进阶梯：从区分漏洞函数与其修复版本，到定位故障并对故障移除作出反应，再到评判经执行验证的代码编辑以及预测具体运行的结果。每个测试都配有一个无需理解能力的基线（例如选取包含风险调用的代码行的规则），并且我们在195个发布于模型训练截止日期之后的漏洞上重复了该研究。研究得出四个发现。首先，区分一个漏洞……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究以程序执行为基准，对515个可重现漏洞设计了五级递进测试，发现LLM漏洞检测器的高基准分数未必代表它们真正理解漏洞，其表现可能与无需理解的简单基线相当。
en_tdlr: Through execution-grounded analysis of 515 reproducible C/C++ vulnerabilities, this study uses a five-level ladder of tests to show that LLM vulnerability detectors' high benchmark scores do not necessarily reflect genuine understanding, as their performance can be matched by understanding-free baselines.
